title: Then more generations came, one after another.
subtitle: History as a long line of peoples
then: After two detailed stories, the surah speeds up. Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}nations and peoples{/idea}, created one after another, {idea}successors after predecessors{/idea}.
now: Your phone shows a photo from ten years ago, and half the people in it have moved on, some have passed away. {idea}Generations turn faster than they seem to.{/idea}
old: My generation is the main event.
new: I am one generation in a long line, each given its turn.
try: Make a dua today for the generation before you and the one after you.

title: No nation can rush its end or delay it.
subtitle: Every term is written
then: Ibn Kathir says they are taken {idea}at the time decreed by Allah in His Book, before they were created{/idea}, nation after nation, century after century. No one can push the date forward or back.
now: You plan the five-year career, the mortgage term, the retirement age. {idea}Your own term is written too, and you cannot see the date.{/idea} Plans are fine. Assuming time is not.
old: I can count on having the time I have planned for.
new: My time is set by Allah, so I use what I have well.
try: Do one thing today that you have been saving for when you have more time.

title: Messenger after messenger, and nations became stories.
subtitle: What is left of those who denied
then: Ibn Abbas said the messengers came {idea}following one another in succession{/idea}. Each time, most of the people denied. Allah destroyed them and {trap}made them stories and lessons for mankind{/trap}.
now: Someday you will be a story told at a dinner table: what grandpa was like, how she treated people. {idea}Every life ends up as a story. You are writing yours now.{/idea}
old: What people say about me after I am gone does not matter.
new: My life will become a story, and I choose today what kind.
try: Write one sentence you would want your family to say about you. Do one thing toward it.

title: Musa and Harun came with signs and clear proof.
subtitle: Two brothers sent with authority
then: Allah sent Musa and Harun {idea}with decisive evidence and definitive proof{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes that the problem was never a lack of signs. Musa was not sent alone: {reward}his brother stood with him.{/reward}
now: You keep saying you will change when you are sure, when you have more evidence. {idea}Sometimes the evidence is already enough, and what is missing is the willingness.{/idea}
old: I just need more proof before I commit.
new: The proof is often clear; the real question is my heart.
try: Name one good step you already know is right. Stop waiting for more proof and take it.

title: Pharaoh's court was too proud to listen.
subtitle: Arrogance as the real barrier
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}Pharaoh and his people were too arrogant to follow them and obey their commands{/trap}, because Musa and Harun were human beings, {idea}just as previous nations had denied{/idea}. Same mentality, different century.
now: Your teenager corrects your grammar. A junior colleague has a better idea in the meeting. {trap}Something in you bristles before you even think.{/trap} {idea}That bristle is where pride lives.{/idea}
old: I am not arrogant; I just know better.
new: Pride can hide inside the feeling that I am above being told.
try: Accept one correction today without defending yourself. Just say thank you.

title: Their people serve us, so why follow them?
subtitle: Looking down on the messenger's people
then: Pharaoh's chiefs said: {trap}should we believe two men like ourselves, while their people serve us in humility?{/trap} The Children of Israel were their laborers. To accept Musa would mean taking guidance from the class they ruled.
now: The cleaner who prays on time. The delivery driver who says bismillah. The refugee neighbor who is more generous than you. {idea}Guidance does not care about the org chart.{/idea}
old: I learn from people above me, not below.
new: Truth can come from anyone, especially those I overlook.
try: Learn one thing today from someone you would normally consider beneath your notice.

title: They denied both brothers and joined the destroyed.
subtitle: The end of Pharaoh's court
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}Allah destroyed Pharaoh and his chiefs, drowning them all in one day{/trap}. The greatest power of its age joined the list of those who were destroyed, {idea}seized by the All-Mighty, All-Capable{/idea}.
now: Some things in your life feel too big to ever fall: a habit, a fear, a grip someone has on you. {idea}Allah ended an empire in one day.{/idea} He can loosen what holds you.
old: Some powers are just too strong to be changed.
new: No power is permanent before Allah, not even the grip of my own habits.
try: Name one habit you think is too strong to break. Ask Allah for help with it tonight.

title: After the rescue came the Book, so they might be guided.
subtitle: Freedom, then guidance
then: Ibn Kathir says after destroying Pharaoh, Allah gave Musa {idea}the Torah, with rulings, commands and prohibitions{/idea}. He cites another verse: an {reward}enlightenment, guidance and mercy, that they might remember{/reward}.
now: You got through the hard year: the illness, the job loss, the breakup. Now there is space. {idea}What you fill that space with is the next chapter.{/idea}
old: Once the trouble ends, I can relax and drift.
new: After Allah rescues me, it is time to be guided, not to drift.
try: After your next relief, set a small new habit with the Quran, even one verse a day.

title: Maryam and her son became a sign, and Allah sheltered them.
subtitle: A miracle and a safe high ground
then: Ibn Kathir says Isa and Maryam were made {idea}a proof of Allah's ability to do what He wills{/idea}. Then {reward}Allah gave them refuge on high ground with rest and flowing water{/reward}. He says the most apparent meaning is Jerusalem, linking it to the stream under Maryam.
now: A single mother carrying gossip and stares. A family that had to leave home and start again. {idea}The verse names both the trial and the shelter.{/idea} Allah does not raise someone as a sign and then abandon them.
old: If people talk about me, Allah must be against me.
new: Allah can make me a sign and still shelter me through it.
try: Check in today on someone who is carrying people's judgment. Offer them a kind word.

title: Eat what is good, then do good.
subtitle: Lawful food feeds righteous deeds
then: Ibn Kathir says eating lawful food {idea}helps one do righteous deeds{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah is good and only accepts what is good, then described a traveller raising his hands, {trap}but his food, drink and clothing are unlawful, so how can he be answered?{/trap} Every Prophet worked; Dawud ate from his own hands.
now: The shortcut at work that bends the truth on an invoice. The extra hour claimed but not worked. {trap}The money buys groceries, and the groceries feed the hands you raise in dua.{/trap}
old: How I earn and how I pray are separate things.
new: What I earn feeds my body, and my body is what I pray with.
try: Look at one source of your income and make sure it is fully honest this week.

title: All the Prophets share one religion and one Lord.
subtitle: One community, one call
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}your religion, O Prophets, is one religion and one group: the call to worship Allah alone with no partner.{/idea} Then: {reward}I am your Lord, so be mindful of Me.{/reward}
now: The family debate about whose masjid is better. The online argument about which teacher is right. {idea}Step back far enough and every Prophet is standing in the same row.{/idea}
old: My little group is the whole of the truth.
new: I belong to one long community of Prophets and believers.
try: Say something kind today about a Muslim who practices a little differently from you.

title: They split into factions, each happy with its own.
subtitle: Division and self-satisfaction
then: Ibn Kathir says the nations to whom Prophets were sent {trap}broke their religion into sects{/trap}, and {trap}each rejoiced in its misguidance because it thought it was rightly guided{/trap}. The comfort itself was the problem.
now: You share a clip that mocks people who think differently, and feel good about it. {trap}That warm feeling of being on the right team{/trap} is exactly what the verse warns about. {idea}The question points at your own heart.{/idea}
old: Feeling sure of my side means I am right.
new: Rejoicing in my side is not proof; sincere checking is.
try: Before sharing anything that mocks another group, pause and ask what it does to your own heart.

title: Leave them in their confusion for a while.
subtitle: A respite that is not approval

row.title: nothing happens, so it is fine

then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to leave them in their error {trap}until the appointed time{/trap}. Ibn Kathir links it to: {idea}let them eat and enjoy and be distracted by hope; they will come to know.{/idea}
now: You know something in your life is off, but nothing bad has happened yet, so you leave it. {idea}Quiet is not the same as approval.{/idea} The respite is a gift to use, not a sign to keep going.
old: If nothing bad has happened, I must be fine.
new: Time without consequence is a chance to turn back, not a green light.
try: Name one thing you keep doing only because nothing has gone wrong yet. Start changing it today.

title: Do they think wealth and children prove Allah loves them?
subtitle: Mistaking gifts for approval
then: Ibn Kathir asks: {trap}do these deceived people think what We give them is because they are honored in Our sight?{/trap} He cites: it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us, {idea}but only whoever believes and does righteous deeds.{/idea}
now: The pay rise, the new baby, the house with a garden. A voice inside says: Allah must be pleased with me. {idea}Maybe. But the gift is not the proof. What you do with it is.{/idea}
old: Blessings in my life mean Allah is pleased with me.
new: Blessings are a test; faith and deeds are what bring me near.
try: Take one blessing you have and use it for someone else's good today.

title: We hasten good things for them? No, they do not perceive.
subtitle: The world is given to all; faith only to the loved
then: The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}Allah gives the world to those He loves and those He does not, but gives religion only to those He loves.{/reward} So the verse says: {trap}they do not perceive{/trap} what their wealth really means.
now: You scroll past someone's holiday, car, wedding, and feel left behind. {idea}If you have faith in your heart, you were given the gift Allah gives only to those He loves.{/idea}
old: Others are more blessed because they have more.
new: If I have faith, I already hold the gift that counts most.
try: When you next feel envious online, close the app and thank Allah for your faith by name.
